title: Nonlinearity
summary: A map is nonlinear when it fails the defining linearity conditions of additivity and scalar homogeneity.

context.note: Framework is named textually in this seed release; full recursive first-principles closure remains future work.

assumptions.text: Vector spaces and a map f between them are specified.

content.plain: In a nonlinear system, combining inputs need not combine outputs by simple superposition.
content.exact: A map f:V→W is linear iff f(ax+by)=af(x)+bf(y) for all x,y and scalars a,b. It is nonlinear if this condition fails.
content.example: f(x)=x^2 on R is nonlinear because f(x+y) generally differs from f(x)+f(y).
content.caveat: Nonlinearity alone does not imply complexity, instability, or chaos.

relations.note: Nonlinear feedback can produce sensitivity, but does not guarantee it.
Nonlinear objectives can create multiple local extrema.
